title: autotune: default batching/caching heuristics, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Add autotune defaults for batching and KV caching, introduce quantization profile catalog and integrate unit-econ estimator into Redwood Console/CLI. Improves token cost by ~12%-45% depending on workload; no API surface breaking changes.
description: Motivation: Customers repeatedly ask for safe, production-ready defaults that reduce per-token cost without manual tuning. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: (1) default automatic batching and KV cache heuristics that adapt to sequence length distribution and customer latency SLO, (2) a quantization profile catalog and runtime selection logic to pick the best quantized model variant per workload, and (3) a unit-economics estimator surfaced in the Console and CLI to show cost/latency trade-offs for a given routing/policy config. Changes are backward-compatible: defaults are opt-in per-tenant for the first rollout, with an account-level toggle and a gradual canary rollout. What changed: - Serving runtime: new autotune controller that observes request histograms, live latency percentiles, and token-level cost to compute per-route targets; new continuous-batching heuristic with dynamic batch size caps; KV cache aggressiveness score computation and TTL defaults tuned for LLM chat workloads. - Quantization: add quant_profile metadata, three curated profiles (fast-8, balanced-4, high-quality-8/4 hybrid), profile selection logic in model catalog and runtime fallback (if a chosen quantized variant fails, runtime falls back to fp16). - Tooling: Console: unit-econ estimator page and per-route recommendation; CLI: redwood autotune simulate --profile to run offline workload estimates; API: additional fields in /v1/routes (autotune.enabled, autotune.last_run). - Telemetry: new metrics (autotune.recommendations.count, quant.profile_usage, uecon.estimated_savings) and dashboards. Rollout plan: enable for internal staging tenants 2026-02-15, beta on opt-in tenants 2026-02-20, full opt-out migration completed by 2026-03-10. Testing: unit tests for controller logic, integration tests with a local model runner and quantized binaries, perf benchmark harness runs included. Related: ENG-1245 (autotune controller), ENG-1290 (qe profiles), SUP-567 (customer ask).

review_comments: Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Nice overall. A few questions about safety: how do we bound worst-case latency when the controller increases batch size?

Author (Ava Chen): We add a hard tail-latency cap per-tenant derived from their route.slo_p99. The controller never proposes a configuration that would violate that cap; see runtime/batching/estimator.rs where cap calculation references route.slo_p99.
Priya Patel (reviewer): We need clearer observability for when a quantized variant is selected vs fallback. Can we emit a metric with tags for model+profile?
Author (Ava Chen): Added quant.profile_usage metric and included model/profile labels in catalog/service.go. Also added a Grafana panel in observability/dashboards/autotune.json.
Diego Ramirez (reviewer): CI perf job failing intermittently in the balanced-4 benchmarks (timeout). Can we increase timeout and add retries?
Author (Ava Chen): Increased perf job timeout and added 2 retries for flaky benchmark infra. Re-ran perf job; results stable.
Priya Patel (approver): Approved after minor doc clarifications. LGTM.
Liam O'Connor (approver): Approved. Verified staging tenant rollout metrics look good.
ROI_estimate: Estimated per-token savings across customers: median 18% (chat workloads), up to 45% for high-locality workloads using fast-8 and KV caching. Payback for engineering effort expected within 6-10 weeks for mid-size tenants.
testing_instructions: Run make test-autotune to execute unit+integration tests. To simulate tenant data: cli/cmd/autotune.go provides 'simulate' that accepts a workload trace (see examples/recipes/autotune_recommendation.md). Staging rollout: toggle account.autotune.enabled via internal admin console, monitor autotune.recommendations.count and uecon.estimated_savings dashboards.
notes: Opt-in rollout + account-level toggle used to avoid customer surprise. No user-facing API breaking changes. We coordinated with Support (SUP-567) for early adopters.
changelog_entry: Autotune defaults: adaptive batching and KV cache heuristics, quantization profile selection, and unit-econ estimator in Console/CLI. Improvements aim to reduce per-token cost with controlled latency behavior.
